newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end down as local investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end down as local investors take profits.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Tuesday as local investors took profits following Monday's highest overall market rise of the year, brokers said.
Prices were seen broadly stable Wednesday despite expectations some players would continue to take profits, they added.

Tuesday, the General Index fell 2.12 percent to 2,167.0 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 2.11 percent to 3,131.0 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
In a total of 2,950 trades, volume was a healthy 54.5 million soles ($20.6 million), brokers said.

The government's announcement Tuesday of a 13.4 percent year-on-year gross domestic product (GDP) rise in April -- the largest monthly jump since February 1995 -- was discounted by investors, who received reports of such a figure Monday, brokers said.

"Local investors were waiting for confirmation of the good figures to go and take profits. But the most important thing is that foreign investors have maintained their positions," Luis Calderon of local brokerage Acciones y Valores said.
Peru's largest brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA fell 2.90 percent to 2.68 soles on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- dropped 0.67 percent to 1.49 soles, on volume of 1.8 million shares.
Cement company Cementos Lima closed unchanged at 5.55 soles on volume of 347,000 shares.
